# Using this skill library from Qwen Code

The working rules, skills and roles you were given were written for Claude Code. They hold here too, with
these translations.

- **Claude Code features you don't have:** every role and the rule sheet start with a note saying so. The
  text below lists the ones found in the library with what to use instead, but it can't name every one: where
  an instruction depends on a tool, mode, command or setting you don't have, skip that part and say so in your
  hand-back rather than improvising it.
- **Skills:** with a `skill` tool, load one by name when the work matches its description. Inside Qwen Code's
  execution sandbox you have none: SKILLS.md in your instructions lists each skill's description and file, so
  read that file with your read tool before starting the work it describes. "Load the X skill" means either.
- **Folder rule files (a known limitation):** Qwen Code reads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md only from the folder it was
  started in and that folder's parents, once, at start. A subfolder's or another folder's rule file is never
  loaded, and an instruction to read it first did not work: in 3 of 3 test runs (Qwen3-Coder-Next, 2026-10-08)
  the agent wrote into a subfolder without reading its AGENTS.md. The workaround is to start the agent in the
  folder it works in. If your task still takes you into another folder that has its own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md,
  read it before changing anything there and say in your report that you did.
- **Your identity:** commit as `local-agent <local-agent@forge.local>` (set in your environment). Where a project's
  CLAUDE.md or a role says to commit as the user, under the user's name, or with "the project's identity", that
  is for Claude Code sessions: don't set `user.name`/`user.email`, `--author` or `-c user.*` to anyone else, or
  change the `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables.
  Keep the commit trailer, naming your own model.
- **Full or core rules:** this file is loaded with the full rule sheet (`--install`, or `--install --rules full`:
  the default until the 2026-10-08 agent-capability A/B test decides). `--install --rules core` loads instead the
  core sheet (`local-agents/qwen/AGENTS-core.md`, under 450 tokens: the rules every role keeps) and
  core-mode roles (`local-agents/qwen/agents-core/`, each with its own core rules and the identity rule); this file,
  the full sheet (~/.qwen/AGENTS-full.md) and SKILLS.md are then read when needed. Both are generated from
  `docs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv` (its `core` and `scope` columns) by `tools/gen_local_agents.py`; don't edit them.
- **Role agents** (designer, developer, qa, ...): start one with the `agent` tool (`subagent_type` = the role's
  name). Each role keeps the tool set its Claude Code file gives it; a role without edit tools cannot edit.
- **`@/path/file.md` lines** in a CLAUDE.md are Claude Code imports; the library's rule sheet is loaded separately.
- **Claude Code tool names** in the text, and yours:

| Claude Code | Qwen Code |
|---|---|
| Read | read_file |
| Edit | edit |
| Write | write_file |
| NotebookEdit | notebook_edit |
| Glob | glob, list_directory |
| Grep | grep_search |
| Bash | run_shell_command |
| WebFetch | web_fetch |
| WebSearch | web_search |
| Skill | skill |
| Agent | agent |
| Task | agent |
| TodoWrite | todo_write |

## Claude-specific text, and how to read it

- **claude-md**: A folder's CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md) is its rule file. Qwen Code loads only the ones in the folder it was started in and that folder's parents, once, at start; nothing loads a subfolder's or another folder's when you work there, and being told to read them first proved unreliable (3 of 3 test runs didn't). So the person starting you starts you in the folder you work in. If your task takes you into another folder that has its own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, read it before changing anything there and say in your report that you did. Where a line says CLAUDE.md arrives by itself or not to open it, that is Claude Code's behaviour: here, do read it. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is Claude Code's machine file; yours are ~/.qwen/AGENTS.md (this rule sheet) and ~/.qwen/CLAUDE.md (machine facts). Appears in: `AGENTS.md` (3), `agents/developer.md` (2), `agents/merge-reviewer.md` (1), `agents/qa.md` (1), `agents/team-ops.md` (2), `agents/tech-lead.md` (1), `agents/writer.md` (1), `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (4), `skills/directing/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/durable-knowledge/SKILL.md` (8), `skills/gamedev-team-practices/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/ground-truth/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/landing/SKILL.md` (1).
- **claude-home**: Claude Code's user folder. Yours is ~/.qwen: the rule sheet ~/.qwen/AGENTS.md, the skills listed in ~/.qwen/SKILLS.md, the roles in ~/.qwen/agents/, session logs under ~/.qwen/projects/<project>/. Appears in: `AGENTS.md` (2), `agents/team-ops.md` (1), `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/durable-knowledge/SKILL.md` (5), `skills/ground-truth/SKILL.md` (1).
- **dot-claude**: A project's .claude/ folder holds Claude Code's per-project roles and skills. Qwen Code reads .qwen/agents/ and .qwen/skills/ (or .agents/skills/) instead. Appears in: `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (1).
- **claude-code**: Describes Claude Code itself: background, not how this tool behaves. Appears in: `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/durable-knowledge/SKILL.md` (2).
- **scratchpad**: Claude Code gives each session a scratch folder (the session scratchpad); `scratchpad/<task>/` means your task's folder in it. You have no scratchpad: use the per-task folder your brief names; if it names none, use `scratch/<task>/` in the folder you were started in (the sandbox refuses writes outside it), don't commit it, and give its absolute path in your report. Appears in: `agents/designer.md` (1), `agents/developer.md` (1), `agents/director.md` (1), `agents/merge-reviewer.md` (3), `agents/presentation.md` (1), `agents/psychologist.md` (3), `agents/publishing.md` (1), `agents/qa.md` (2), `agents/team-ops.md` (1), `agents/tech-lead.md` (1), `agents/writer.md` (1), `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (3), `skills/directing/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/psychology-review/SKILL.md` (1).
- **slash-command**: A word starting with `/`: a path (the library's hits, /tmp and the `AudioStreamWAV`/playback pair, are these) or a Claude Code slash command (/compact, /clear, /context), which the user types, not you. Qwen Code's differ (/compress for /compact; /help lists them). Appears in: `skills/durable-knowledge/SKILL.md` (2).
- **compaction**: Claude Code's context compaction (/compact). Qwen Code compresses the chat history near its limit too (/compress by hand); what isn't in a file is lost either way, so the advice holds. Appears in: `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/durable-knowledge/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/ground-truth/SKILL.md` (1).
- **mcp**: Claude Code's MCP servers (.mcp.json). Qwen Code has its own in settings `mcpServers`; this library installs none, so say a tool you'd need is missing. Appears in: `skills/dependency-policy/SKILL.md` (3).
- **claude-feature**: A Claude Code feature, or a word that names one. Subagents are your roles, started with the `agent` tool; plugins, output styles, auto memory and artifacts in the sense of Claude's published pages ("artifacts, external pages") you don't have: say so. The word artifact in its general sense (a file, a build's or deployment's output, the evidence behind a claim) is the library's own and holds as written; so is a build or git hook. Appears in: `AGENTS.md` (1), `agents/presentation.md` (1), `agents/team-ops.md` (1), `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (3), `skills/dependency-policy/SKILL.md` (3), `skills/durable-knowledge/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/generated-art/SKILL.md` (1), `skills/ground-truth/SKILL.md` (7), `skills/migrations/SKILL.md` (1).
- **claude-tool**: A Claude Code tool you don't have: say so rather than improvise one. Appears in: `skills/landing/SKILL.md` (1).
- **agent-setting**: A Claude Code agent setting. Inside Qwen Code's sandbox the `agent` tool refuses worktree agents. Appears in: `skills/agent-team/SKILL.md` (1).
- **session-log**: Claude Code's session-log layout. Qwen Code's: ~/.qwen/projects/<project>/chats/*.jsonl and subagents/<session>/agent-*.jsonl with .meta.json. Appears in: `agents/team-ops.md` (2).
- **identity**: An identity rule. You commit as local-agent <local-agent@forge.local>, never as the user. Appears in: `agents/developer.md` (1).
